tasks.short: Record weather and fuel moisture during the burn, walk the burned area, analyze burn conditions and results, write the postburn report, and send it to the land manager.

steps.what: Fire captain records weather and fuel moisture readings during the burn on paper
Fire captain walks the burned area to assess results
Fire captain analyzes burn conditions and results against the burn plan
Fire captain prepares the postburn report

loop.input: The burn plan, the logged weather and fuel moisture readings, the mapped burned area and the captain's notes.
loop.output: A draft postburn report in the region's template.
loop.check: Code checks every reading, time and area in the text matches the logged data and every plan objective has a result; the captain edits and approves.
loop.stop: Stops when the checks pass and the captain approves, or after two failed redrafts the captain writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: What went well and what to change needs prose; a template only fills in the numbers.

steps.what: Fire captain e-mails the postburn report to the land manager

tasks.design: A portable weather station logs wind, humidity and temperature during the burn, and fuel moisture readings go into a form on the tablet ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the captain stops writing readings on paper. The burned perimeter is walked with the tablet's GPS. A bounded step drafts the postburn report from the plan, the logged readings and the captain's notes; code checks every number, and the captain edits. Once approved, the report goes to the land manager. Walking the area and judging results stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were written on paper and reports typed from scratch weeks later.
tasks.enabler_now: Portable weather stations log readings; tablets map perimeters; language models draft reports from structured data.
tasks.still_hard: Effects on vegetation show only months later.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a patchy burn was the weather or the crew's ignition pattern.
tasks.altitude: The captain edits reports instead of typing them.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive before the next burn is planned.

evidence.claim: Portable weather stations log readings; language models can draft reports from structured data with numbers checked by code.

assumptions: Boundary: from the burn plan to the report sent; vegetation monitoring in later years is outside.
Input contract: burn plan from the region; readings from the weather station; fallback is paper and typing.
Walking the area and judging results do not change.
No personal data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the drafted report does the captain change?

already_counted.description: Fire captain edits and approves the drafted report.

incremental.description: Fire captain sets up and checks the weather station before the burn.

approvals.approved_version: The postburn report as edited and approved by the captain in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small burn with few readings; high: a large burn over several units.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the inspection from the permit file, take part in inspections of properties, supervise the inspectors, record findings, decide on compliance and check the findings letter, and send it to the owner.

steps.what: Fire captain prepares the inspection from the permit file and earlier findings
Fire captain participates in the inspection of properties for compliance with fire codes
Fire captain supervises the inspectors on site
Fire captain records findings on the paper checklist and types them up
Fire captain decides on compliance and checks the findings letter
Fire captain posts the findings letter to the property owner

tasks.design: The inspection app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows the permit, drawings and earlier findings per address, and the checklist on the tablet names the code article behind each item, so findings are recorded once on site with photos. The findings letter fills from the recorded items with their articles. Once the captain has decided on compliance and checked the letter, it goes to the owner. Inspecting, supervising inspectors and deciding stay with the captain; inspection times are not used to rate inspectors.
tasks.previous_blocker: Permit files sat in archives, findings went on paper and letters were typed afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Inspection apps with checklists linked to code articles are common in safety regions and municipalities.
tasks.still_hard: Older buildings rarely match their drawings.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a blocked escape route is a habit, not an accident.

reach.learn: Whether letters go out the same week.

evidence.claim: Inspection apps can show permit files and link checklist items to code articles.
Systems that can monitor staff, such as time-stamped inspection logs, need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the inspection planning to the letter sent; enforcement proceedings are outside.
Input contract: permit files from the municipality's archive; checklists kept by the region; fallback is paper.
Inspecting and deciding do not change.
Owners receive the letter as they do today; no added owner time.
research_questions: Do repeat inspections find fewer open items?

incremental.description: Fire captain reports outdated checklist items.

approvals.approved_version: The findings letter as checked by the captain in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few inspections with simple buildings; high: many inspections of complex buildings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the burn plan, coordinate with the land manager, neighbours and dispatch centre, decide go or no-go on the day, notify those involved, and direct and supervise the burn.

steps.what: Fire captain plans prescribed burn projects in a burn plan
Fire captain coordinates with the land manager, neighbours and the dispatch centre
Fire captain decides go or no-go on the day from the weather forecast
Fire captain phones the dispatch centre and neighbours that the burn starts
Fire captain directs and supervises the prescribed burn

tasks.design: Burn plans start from the region's template ({DOCS}) with map, objectives, weather limits and crew pre-filled from the last burn of that unit. A shared contact list holds the land manager, neighbours and dispatch centre; once the captain decides go, one message tells all of them the burn starts. Agreeing with the land manager, deciding go or no-go and directing the burn stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were written from scratch and everyone was phoned on the morning of the burn.
tasks.enabler_now: Plan templates and group messages are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: The weather window can close within an hour.
tasks.human_edge: Calling off a burn when the wind turns, even after weeks of planning.

reach.learn: Whether calls about smoke from planned burns fall.

evidence.claim: Plan templates and group messages can replace building plans from scratch and calling contacts one by one.

assumptions: Boundary: from the burn request to the burn completed; the postburn report is outside.
Input contract: requests from the land manager; contacts kept by the region; fallback is phone calls.
Deciding go or no-go and directing the burn do not change.
Neighbours read the message in about the time a call took; no added neighbour time.
research_questions: Do smoke reports to the dispatch centre fall?

incremental.description: Fire captain keeps the contact list current.

approvals.approved_version: The go decision taken by the captain in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one burn unit with few neighbours; high: repeat burns over many units.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find the fire safety codes and guidelines that apply, study and interpret them, write the permit procedure for hazardous substances, check it with the legal advisor, publish it, and brief permit officers.

steps.what: Fire captain finds the fire safety codes and guidelines that apply to the substances
Fire captain studies and interprets fire safety codes for hazardous or flammable substances
Fire captain writes the procedure and checklist for issuing permits

loop.input: The captain's interpretation notes and the texts of the applicable codes and guidelines.
loop.output: Draft procedure steps and checklist items, each with the article it relies on.
loop.check: Code checks every quoted article text appears in the current version of the code or guideline; items without a matching quote are dropped; the captain edits and approves.
loop.stop: Stops when every item has a matching quote and the captain approves, or after two failed redrafts the captain writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning code articles into permit steps needs interpretation in prose; a search only finds the articles.

steps.what: Fire captain checks the procedure with the legal advisor
Fire captain e-mails the procedure to the permit team
Fire captain briefs permit officers on the new procedure

tasks.design: Current codes and guidelines sit in one searchable document system ({DOCS}) with versions, so the captain finds the articles that apply without searching several sites. A bounded step drafts procedure steps and checklist items from the captain's interpretation; code checks every quoted article against the current text, and the captain edits. Once checked with the legal advisor, the procedure is published to the permit team in the document system. Interpreting the codes stays with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Codes were searched on several sites and procedures written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems hold current code texts; language models draft procedure text from notes.
tasks.still_hard: Guidelines change and older procedures go out of date.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which storage rule a small business can really meet.
tasks.altitude: The captain interprets and edits instead of searching and writing from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether the procedure cuts questions back to the fire service.

evidence.claim: Safety regions apply PGS 15 for stored hazardous substances in permit procedures; version 1.1 dates from April 2026.
Language models can draft procedure text from notes, with quotes checked against source texts by code.

assumptions: Boundary: from the permit question to the officers briefed; issuing permits is outside.
Input contract: code texts from the publishers; fallback is searching their sites.
Interpreting codes and checking with the legal advisor do not change.
The legal advisor's time does not change.
research_questions: How many drafted items does the captain drop?

already_counted.description: Fire captain edits and approves drafted procedure items.

incremental.description: Fire captain checks procedures when a guideline changes.

approvals.approved_version: The procedure as checked with the legal advisor in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small change to an existing procedure; high: a new procedure for a new substance class.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fire captain keeps judging burns, inspecting, deciding go or no-go and interpreting codes; paper readings, typed reports, phone rounds and code searches shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A captain with more time on site and with the crew.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Firefighting and Prevention Workers
